sections.p: Tuesday's US session sold gold off from 4,193 (8:30 AM ET) to 4,148 (1:50 PM ET), settling near 4,162 – a second straight down day, roughly 0.8% lower over two sessions.

Gold opened at 4,163 at 6:00 PM ET and slipped to the Asian low of 4,145 at 9:45 PM ET before bouncing to the Asian high of 4,172 at 11:15 PM ET – about five hours after the open – on dovish comments from the NY Fed's Williams. Sellers then picked the prior move back up, and Asia closed at 4,149.
High of 4,159 at 4:15 AM ET, low of 4,141 at 6:25 AM ET – the low of the day. Heading into 7:00 AM ET, gold was hovering around 4,138–4,144.

A slightly softer dollar (DXY ~102.1) and long-end Treasury yields down 3–4 bps kept the slide contained. But Brent above $106 on renewed Middle East attacks revived inflation worries. Williams sees one more hike this year but none in 2027, while Waller and Goolsbee leaned hawkish on AI-driven price pressure. Markets price roughly 90% odds of a December hike – higher rates remain the main headwind for gold.
September CPI at 8:30 AM ET: headline est. 3.6% y/y; core est. +0.2% m/m and 2.5% y/y. A hot print would lift the dollar and yields and pressure gold; a soft one would support a bounce.

Price is below MA34 (4,162) and MA89 (4,176), hugging the lower BB90 (2 SD) at 4,142 (mid 4,176, upper 4,211). Daily pivots: P 4,171 · R1 4,194 · S1 4,139 · S2 4,116. Into the NY open, expect chop between 4,139 and 4,163 until CPI: a hot core print could break S1 toward 4,116; a soft one could lift price back to 4,162–4,171.

scenarios_en: US calendar (ET, ForexFactory): no tier-1 data Tuesday Oct 13 · CPI Wed Oct 14, 8:30 AM ET (f'cast 3.6% y/y, core 2.5%) · PPI + retail sales Thu Oct 15, 8:30 AM ET · Fed Chair Warsh speaks Thu Oct 15, 11:30 PM ET.
Into CPI (Oct 13 – early Oct 14 ET): below 4,202 → favor selling rallies, targets 4,178 then 4,170; a break of 4,170 opens 4,128. Holding above 4,205 → bounce toward 4,228–4,242.
After CPI (Wed 8:30 AM ET) – hotter than expected (above 3.6%): dollar and yields up, stronger Fed-hike bets → gold likely breaks 4,170 toward 4,128–4,091.
After CPI – softer than expected: gold can pop quickly to 4,242–4,259; only call it a reversal on a daily close above 4,260 (daily 20 EMA at 4,249).
No new entries 5 minutes either side of a release; wait for an M15 close to confirm before working the zones.
strategies.physicalAdvice_en: Bigger picture, gold is in a long, deep downtrend and could go meaningfully lower over the medium to long term. Physical buyers may want to be patient and wait for a better entry.
macro_en: CNBC/Reuters (Oct 12): early in Asia spot gold rose to $4,206/oz, its highest since Oct 2, on softer oil and the dollar after the Russia–Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' announcement; it then cooled as the market waits on Wednesday's CPI.

FXStreet (3:08 PM ET Oct 12): XAU/USD down about 1.5% at $4,163; WTI above $93 after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Iran hitting ships in Hormuz – the 'oil → inflation → rates' channel is bearish for gold.
DXY up 0.3% at 102.56; the 10-year Treasury yield 5.242% – high rates keep weighing on gold (FXStreet).
Markets price ~20% odds of a 25 bp Fed hike at the Oct 27–28 meeting and nearly 90% by December (FXStreet citing Prime Terminal). Current range 3.75–4.00% (Fed, Sep 16).
